questions.q: What ties the lab's three research projects together, according to this lesson?
options: They all use the same reinforcement learning algorithm
They're all built around SQL and data systems instead of generic game or text tasks
They all train the exact same base model
They all run on the same cloud provider
questions.explain: Rather than generic game or text-only RL tasks, all three projects are deliberately built around SQL and data systems, this catalog's own strength.

questions.q: What is Project 3's deliverable, by name?
options: An optimizer hint classifier
A Northwind data-cleaning rubric
"SQL Pete," a natural-language-to-SQL assistant
A reward model for query plans
questions.explain: Project 3 fine-tunes a small open-weight model into "SQL Pete," a natural-language-to-SQL assistant, then runs RLHF on top of it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend keeping a research notebook from the very first experiment?
options: Because a research project has no answer key, so you're the one deciding what counts as evidence
Because the course platform requires one for a passing grade
Because it's a substitute for writing any code
Because notebooks are only useful after a project succeeds
questions.explain: Unlike a graded course module with a known answer, a research project requires you to decide what counts as evidence — a dated notebook is how you track that reasoning as it happens.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should you do with a dead end in your research notebook?
options: Delete it so the notebook only shows successful attempts
Record it — a documented dead end is still a finding
Move it to a separate private file
Wait until the project ends to mention it
questions.explain: Dead ends belong in the notebook too; a documented dead end is still a finding, and it's exactly what each project's write-up asks you to summarize.

questions.q: What happens in Chapter 5, between Project 3 and the final wrap-up chapter?
options: A fourth independent research project with its own new model
A repeat of Project 1 at larger scale
An interpretability case study that inspects the model built in Project 3
A graded exam covering all three projects
questions.explain: Chapter 5 is an interpretability case study on SQL Pete, the model built in Project 3, before the lab wraps up in Chapter 6.
